leads.summary: Stop mistakes a real tmux socket error for an idle remote machine
leads.consequence: tmux 3.7c prints `error connecting to <socket> (Permission denied)` for EACCES (and the same prefix for other failures). The broad `*error connecting*` exits 0 before emitting a tagged failure; the local command tells the user `No agent session is running`, although it could not inspect or stop any. The original failure-handling complaint is only partially addressed. Match the actual no-server errno, and report other errors.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (judged unrealistic: default socket dir is per-uid 0700 and tmux reports unsafe permissions first); not published

leads.summary: Explicit empty stop argument is treated as stop-all
leads.consequence: `omarchy agent stop "$session"` with an empty session variable (or `omarchy agent stop ""`) silently takes the no-argument branch, kills every `omarchy-agent-*` session, reports success and leaves no way to resume those jobs. The test only exercises omitted argument and a nonempty name. Reject an explicitly supplied empty session, distinguish `$#` from `${1:-}`.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed at bin/omarchy-agent-stop:24-29 (-n ${1:-} test); minor edge, not published

leads.summary: Stop-all also kills manually created tmux sessions with the reserved-looking prefix
leads.consequence: The script promises only to kill sessions the launcher started, but matches names alone. A manually created `tmux new-session -s omarchy-agent-notes` is killed by unqualified stop; such sessions are not tracked as launcher-owned. A naming convention cannot prove ownership. Limit the promise, or tag sessions with a tmux user option and filter on it.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed; unlikely naming collision, not published

leads.summary: Remote OpenClaw requires Omarchy's launcher on the far machine, not just OpenClaw
leads.consequence: On a non-Omarchy remote with an installed `openclaw` executable but no `omarchy-launch-openclaw`, the preflight prints that the Omarchy helper is not installed and never runs OpenClaw. The manual currently says only that the agent needs installing on the remote. Explain the helper dependency or provide a direct OpenClaw TUI path when the gateway is already configured.
leads.triage: factual; deliberate and commented in code (launcher checked as well as agent); pre-existing design, not a regression; not published

leads.summary: Pending configurable agent-directory PR still disagrees with remote working directory
leads.consequence: Open PR #9350 sets local launches from home to the configured directory, but this PR's remote script continues to choose remote `~/Work`. Both edits merge in bin/omarchy-agent without a textual conflict, so a user selecting `omarchy default agent-directory ~/Projects` gets different projects for local and remote runs. This is the outstanding related-PR N7, not a newly introduced head regression; coordinate a remote-directory policy before both merge.
leads.triage: duplicate of prior N7; acknowledged by author; mentioned as noted

leads.summary: Stop's SSH mock still cannot catch stdin draining
leads.consequence: The mock SSH uses only its last argument and never touches stdin. Deleting stop's `</dev/null` therefore leaves every new stop test green, while a real SSH would duplicate and forward caller stdin. Add a piped-stdin negative control whose remaining data is asserted after stop, or make the SSH mock read stdin. This was prior optional N6 and remains a test gap, not proof that the current implementation drains stdin.
leads.triage: duplicate of prior N6 theme; current code correct and remote script reads no stdin; not published

limits: The published test mock substitutes Bash for the remote account's login shell and does not start real tmux panes; source inspection of fish 3.7.1 and tmux 3.7c was used for quoting/argv premises. No real SSH was used.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at head `201ae2a5`, checking the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12059#issuecomment-5858285878) against the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12059#issuecomment-5860178281).

**Verified:** every earlier finding is addressed. The PR's real launcher and stop scripts were run against a simulated far side (bash, real tmux 3.7c, Omarchy's `tmux.conf`), with the previous head `136b0078` as a control:

| Earlier finding | Previous head | `201ae2a5` |
|---|---|---|
| Second prompted launch | attached to `omarchy-agent-Work`, prompt dropped | new `omarchy-agent-claude-Work-2` with the prompt |
| Default agent switched to codex | attached to the old session, codex never started | new `omarchy-agent-codex-Work` running codex with the prompt |
| Unprompted launch while a session runs | attached | attached, no second agent |
| ssh command line | `bash -lic $'...'` | `bash -lic 'eval "$(printf %s <base64> \| base64 -d)"'`, no quote or backslash inside the single quotes |
| tmux layer | one string, parsed by `default-shell` | separate words, run without a shell (tmux `spawn.c`) |
| `omarchy default agent` | printed help | prints the current agent |
| `omarchy agent stop` with another session running | window moved into that session | window closed |
| stop when tmux reports an error other than no server (an unsafe socket directory) | "No agent session is running", exit 0 | reports the tmux error, exit 1 |

On a bash far side, a prompt with quotes, newlines, backslashes, `!`, `!!`, `$(...)`, backticks, `${HOME}` and tabs reached the agent as one literal argument, and nothing in it ran. The ControlPath now uses `%C` in both launch and stop. The stop example, the mise wording and the agents panel wording are corrected. The test now runs the decoded remote script against a stateful tmux mock, and stop is one ssh call, so the earlier stdin note no longer applies. #9350 is noted in the description. The PR test file passes on the head and on a merge with the current `quattro` tip. `test/shell` fails the same 14 files on `quattro` alone and on the merge.

Three new points came up, one of them caused by the earlier review's own suggestion.

### A prompt ending in `;` loses the semicolon

tmux parses its own command-line arguments, and an argument that ends in `;` ends the tmux command; the `;` is removed (tmux 3.7c `cmd-parse.y`, `cmd_parse_from_arguments`). The agent's argv now reaches `tmux new-session` as separate words ([`bin/omarchy-agent:234`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/201ae2a5543d1e7bdb98d0603e2db6682c9f4a80/bin/omarchy-agent#L234)), and the prompt is always the last word. Run with real tmux:

```text
omarchy agent prompt "Explain this line: x = 1;"     agent received: Explain this line: x = 1
omarchy agent prompt "... backslash-semicolon \;"    agent received: ... backslash-semicolon ;
omarchy agent prompt "no trailing semicolon; here"   agent received: no trailing semicolon; here  (unchanged)
```

The earlier review suggested this separate-words form without accounting for tmux's `;` handling. The previous head passed one quoted string and was not affected.

**Impact:** a final `;` (or the backslash before it) is silently dropped from the prompt. Nothing runs and no second tmux command is formed.

**Suggested change:** escape a trailing `;` in each word handed to tmux. This preserved `x = 1;`, `ends \;`, `plain`, `mid; dle`, `;` and `two;;` with real tmux:

```bash
tmux_argv=()
for word in env "PATH=$PATH" "${command[@]}"; do
  [[ $word == *';' ]] && word=${word%;}'\;'
  tmux_argv+=("$word")
done
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -x "${columns:-80}" -y "${rows:-24}" "${tmux_argv[@]}"
```

The tmux mock in the test does not model this, so a test would need to check the escaped form in the logged `new-session` call.

### The agent key never returns to a numbered session

An unprompted launch only ever attaches to or creates the base session `omarchy-agent-<agent>-<dir>` ([`bin/omarchy-agent:232-238`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/201ae2a5543d1e7bdb98d0603e2db6682c9f4a80/bin/omarchy-agent#L232-L238)). A `-2` session keeps running after its window closes, but the agent key never returns to it:

```text
base session ended, omarchy-agent-claude-Work-2 still running
agent key  ->  creates a new omarchy-agent-claude-Work, starts a fresh claude
               -2 stays detached; two agents now work in ~/Work
```

**Impact:** the manual's promise that the agent key "drops you back into that same session rather than starting a second agent" ([`manual/17-ai.md:43`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/201ae2a5543d1e7bdb98d0603e2db6682c9f4a80/manual/17-ai.md?plain=1#L43)) holds only for the base session. Omarchy has no command that returns to a numbered session: getting back takes tmux's own session switching from another agent window on that host (for example `prefix s`), or a manual `ssh -t <host> tmux attach -t <name>`. `omarchy agent stop <name>` ends it.

**Suggested change:** some possible approaches:
- Document how to reattach a numbered session.
- Let `omarchy agent` take a session name, the way `omarchy agent stop` does.
- Have an unprompted launch attach to the most recent running session for that agent and directory.

### Smaller notes

- **Zero-size terminal:** the size comes from `stty size` and only empty values fall back to 80x24 ([`bin/omarchy-agent:233-234`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/201ae2a5543d1e7bdb98d0603e2db6682c9f4a80/bin/omarchy-agent#L233-L234)). A pty that reports `0 0` gives `-x 0`, which tmux rejects (`width too small`), and the launch exits 1. The previous head attached normally in the same case. Normal terminal windows report a real size, so this is unlikely; treating `0` like an empty value would avoid it.
- **Optional test improvement:** the far-side mock pulls the base64 out with a regex and runs the decoded script, so the `bash -lic 'eval "$(...)"'` wrapper is only pattern-checked. Dropping the double quotes around `$(...)` in the wrapper still passes the whole test file, while a real bash far side then fails with `[[: command not found` and never reaches tmux. Having the mock run the full remote string with `bash -c` would cover the wrapper.

---

**Test scope:** head `201ae2a5`, previous head `136b0078` as a control, and a merge with `quattro` tip `3faafba2`. Source inspection of the changed scripts, the manual, the test and the relevant tmux 3.7c, OpenSSH 10.5p1 and fish 3.7.1 source or documentation. The launch and stop paths were run against a simulated far side (sshd simulated as `bash -c`, bash login shell, real tmux 3.7c with Omarchy's `tmux.conf`), and the PR test file, `test/shell`, `test/cli`, a wrapper mutant and a direct tmux semicolon check were run in an isolated sandbox. `test/cli` stops early at the same environment-dependent assertion with and without the PR. No real ssh connection was made. fish and zsh login shells were not run; the fish conclusion rests on its documentation and the content of the ssh command line. The kill-failure path of `omarchy agent stop` was checked from source only. For the agents panel, only the manual wording was checked; the panel was not rendered.
